title: UHDI
description: Debug information that links an original design (what the frontend declared) to the generated netlist (what the compiler emitted). `original` and `generated` describe the two sides on their own; `bindings` is the only place that links them. The names follow the scopes proposal for source maps: `originalScopes`, `generatedRanges` and their bindings. A reader meets a newer document as follows: it ignores a key it does not know; it shows a type of unknown `kind` as its bits if it has a `width`, otherwise as opaque; it treats an unknown `$` value as `$optimized_out`, and an expression with such an operand as having no value, except for the unselected branch of `?:`; it skips a statement of unknown `kind`. A value has bits of 0 and 1 only as far as the document goes: a reader shows X and Z bits as the simulator reports them, and the document says nothing about them.

uhdi.description: Format version, `<major>.<minor>`. A change that only adds keys, kinds or values raises the minor number; any other change raises the major. A reader checks it before anything else and accepts any minor of a major it knows.

producer.description: Tool that wrote the document. Diagnostic only, like DWARF's DW_AT_producer; readers must not branch on it.

profiles.description: Optional parts of the format the document uses. Listed only when used, so a reader that lacks a profile knows up front what it will not understand.

anyOf.description: Original modules carry `stmts`; bindings carry the generated value of each `when` guard. A statement is where a debugger may stop, like a line-table row flagged `is_stmt` in DWARF.
Statements carry `reads`: the source paths their right-hand side reads.
A language extension. A record object may carry the key `x-<name>` only when `x-<name>` is listed here. The core does not look inside it; a companion schema does, such as `uhdi-x-chisel.schema.json`.

files.description: Every file a location refers to, by index. Original and generated files share one list, so a location is always [file, line, column]. DWARF keeps the same list as `file_names` in the line table header; source maps as `sources`.

path.description: Path as the producer saw it. A relative path resolves against the directory the producer ran in. A reader must not resolve a path outside the directories it is given.

generated.description: Present on files of the emitted netlist. Lets a reader tell a Verilog location from a source one without guessing from the extension.

types.description: Type table, referred to by index. A type comes after the types it is built from. DWARF shares types the same way, as type DIEs that variables refer to.

original.description: Modules the frontend declared, with their variables; DWARF's abstract instance of a subprogram. A module made by lowering, such as a memory, is not here, unless it holds variables the frontend declared: the module a layer block is extracted into is here, marked `artificial`.

generated.description: Modules of the emitted netlist, keyed by their Verilog name.

bindings.description: How the variables of an original module read in a generated module; DWARF's concrete instance with its locations. One original module may bind into several generated ones and back (dedup, inlining). There is at most one binding per (`original`, `generated`, `inline_path`).

loc.description: [file index into `files`, line, column]; line counts from 1. Column counts from 1, as the frontend counts it, and 0 means unknown. The column may be left out.

key.description: Name of a variable or field. It contains none of `.`, `[`, `]`, so a path splits unambiguously.

typeName.description: Source-language name of the type (`UInt<8>`, `Bundle` subclass). Shown to the user; never needed to decode a value.

type.description: Kinds follow FIRRTL ground and aggregate types; the bits of a value are fully described by `kind` with `width`, `fields`, `elem`/`size` or `base`.

kind.description: A clock, when the IR still knows it is one. One bit wide.
A reset, when the IR still knows it is one: `reset` is synchronous, `asyncreset` asynchronous. Both are active-high. One bit wide.

flip.description: The field runs against the aggregate's direction, as FIRRTL `flip`.

base.description: The integer type that holds the encoding.

values.description: Label to encoding. A string holds a value too wide for a JSON number.

kind.description: An instance: the type of a variable that instantiates a module.

module.description: Key into `original`: the module as written, before dedup.

name.description: Source-language class of the instance, such as a Chisel `Module` subclass. Two instances of one module may name different classes.
Source-language class of the module. A debugger uses it when no instance names one, such as for the top module.

artificial.description: Made by the compiler, not written in the source, such as the module a layer block is extracted into; DWARF's `DW_AT_artificial`. A debugger may show its variables in the scope of the module that instantiates it.

vars.description: Variables the module declares, by a name unique in the module. A key contains none of `.`, `[`, `]`.

stmts.description: Profile `stmt`: the module body in source order.

name.description: Name a debugger shows, when it differs from the key. The key stays the identifier that paths use; it may be made unique, such as `x_1` for a second `x`.

storage.description: Present when the source treats the variable as state: `reg` keeps its value between clock edges, `mem` is the contents of a memory, a vector whose elements are read and written by address. The frontend decides it, from a declaration or from how the variable is assigned. A port may be `reg`. Absent for wires and other combinational values. A later minor may add values.

dir.description: Present when the variable is a port of the module; `inout` is a bidirectional port, such as an analog one. For an aggregate, the direction of its unflipped fields, as in FIRRTL; flipped fields run the other way. Never on an instance.

node.description: The variable names an expression, such as a FIRRTL `node`, rather than a declared wire. Never with `storage`.

artificial.description: Made by the compiler, not written in the source, such as an instance of an artificial module.

loc.description: Where the module is declared in the netlist.

kind.description: An external module: declared, not emitted.

signals.description: Where each signal declared in the module body is, by its Verilog name. Ports are not listed. A debugger goes from a variable bound to a signal to the signal's declaration.

generatedModule.description: A Verilog module: where it is written and whether it has a body. Instances are variables of the original modules.

inline_path.description: Instance names from `generated` down to an inlined instance, outermost first. Present only on the binding of an inlined copy.

vars.description: Every variable of the original module, by its key there, to its value in the generated one. The keys are a subset of the original module's vars. A missing key means the variable has no value in this generated module, the same as `$optimized_out`. For `$inst` and `$inline`, the original module of the child is the module named by the variable's type.

stmts.description: Profile `stmt`: `when` id to the generated value of its guard.

value.description: A signal name, a slice of a signal, a literal, an expression, a value optimized away, an instance, or an aggregate of those shaped like the variable's type.

oneOf.description: Name of a signal in the generated module. On a struct or vector it is the whole value, and its layout is not known: a debugger shows the bits. To give the layout, bind each leaf to a `$slice`.
Literal, all bits of the leaf's width, most significant first; a signed value in two's complement. DWARF's `DW_AT_const_value`.
Bits `lo` to `hi` of a signal in the generated module, both included; bit 0 is the least significant. A leaf of an aggregate that the netlist keeps in one signal, such as a packed struct.
Value of a zero-width leaf, which has no bits.
No signal carries the value any more; a debugger shows it as `<optimized out>`, like a DWARF location list with a gap.
Value of an instance kept in Verilog: its instance name there and the generated module it instantiates.
Value of an instance inlined into the generated module: the `inline_path` of the binding that holds its variables. DWARF's `DW_TAG_inlined_subroutine`.
A struct value, field name to value.
A vector value, one element per index.

expr.description: Profile `expr`: the combinational op over generated signals and literals that computes the value; DWARF computes such a value with a `DW_OP_*` expression. Opcodes are Verilog's, as HGLDD uses them. A plain number in `args` is a static operand: the count of `R{}` (first), the high and low bit of `[]` (last). `$signed` marks the operands of a signed op. `^` with one operand is the reduction. `?:` needs a value only in the branch it selects: an unselected branch may be `$optimized_out`, which expresses state shared between FSMs. Any other operator with an operand that has no value has no value.

path.description: Source path from a variable or instance of the module: a name, then `.field`, `[n]` with a decimal index, or `[path]` for a dynamic subscript. The subscript path is names and `.field` only, without nested subscripts.

oneOf.description: A register is declared. Its writes take effect at the next clock edge.

id.description: Unique in the module; key of `bindings[].stmts`.
Unique in the module; key of `bindings[].stmts`.

oneOf.description: A named node: a value computed every cycle from what it reads.

id.description: Unique in the module; key of `bindings[].stmts`.
Unique in the module; key of `bindings[].stmts`.

oneOf.description: A module is instantiated. The instance is the variable `var`; its type names the module.

id.description: Unique in the module; key of `bindings[].stmts`.

var.description: Key into the module's `vars`: the instance variable.

id.description: Unique in the module; key of `bindings[].stmts`.

oneOf.description: Statements under a guard; the guard's generated value is in `bindings[].stmts`.

id.description: Unique in the module; key of `bindings[].stmts`.
